label: early copy steps (outputting 2nd/3rd token) in long sequences
explanation: Positional copy-phase unit. 99% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and 96% of it falls on the first two copy steps after the delimiter (recall_idx 1 and 2, i.e. input orig(0)/orig(1) while outputting orig(1)/orig(2)). Rate and magnitude rise sharply with sequence length: L=9 holds 69% of mass and L=8 holds 20%. The top activations (e.g. u j v c n s r r p <DEL> [u] [j]) are all L=8-9 sequences at these two steps. Never fires in the original phase, rarely at the delimiter, and almost never later in the copy (a small bump at the final step of L=9). Precision is low (~15%): only a minority of eligible steps fire, and which ones fire depends on token identity in a graded way (inputs f, 1, e, q, j, b; outputs m, v, x, z; next outputs a, v, i, o all have elevated rates). No simple token set gives a crisp gate (F1 at most ~0.36).
